headline: High: Flowise’s writable shared workspace and broad egress create dangerous default paths for leakage, cascading errors, and compliance drift when paired with Airflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can emit task outputs and broad network-fetched content, while Flowise can read files and run browser/tool nodes; if Airflow output is copied into Flowise flows or files, prompt-like content can steer downstream behavior. No shared channel is explicit, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are pasted into Flowise prompts or uploaded files
IF Flowise nodes treat file contents as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data split in Flowise prompts
Disable file ingestion for untrusted Airflow outputs
Review one sample DAG output before connecting it to Flowise
Use a read-only staging bucket for Airflow artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and Flowise reads/writes the server filesystem plus handles model-provider and tool credentials. If both touch the same workspace or uploaded files, Flowise can expose Airflow-produced artifacts or secrets to external APIs. The pair’s shared-data path is plausible from profiles alone.
conditions: IF Airflow writes artifacts into a directory Flowise can read
IF Flowise flows send uploaded file contents to model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Move Airflow and Flowise to separate volumes
Remove secrets from any shared upload directory
Inspect one Flowise flow for file-to-LLM edges
Rotate any credentials stored in Flowise after testing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an orchestrator with broad egress, and Flowise supports write_filesystem plus shared_state_with_other_instances via server datastore. If they operate on the same mutable workspace or shared datastore, concurrent writes can overwrite DAG artifacts, flow state, or generated files. The profiles show overlapping write surfaces and no locking guarantee.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF no external lock or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Turn on a single-writer policy for shared paths
Check whether the datastore is shared across instances
Pause one agent during writes for a quick test
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking or leases

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate pipeline outputs that Flowise may consume as tool inputs or prompts, and Flowise’s graph-based flows can act on them with browser and HTTP tools. Without a verification step, a bad Airflow artifact can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or external requests. This interaction is plausible and dangerous in default-style automation.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Airflow-produced text as authoritative input
IF a Flowise node triggers HTTP or browser actions from that input
mitigations: Insert a human review step between Airflow and Flowise
Require schema validation on Airflow outputs
Disable action-taking nodes for the first run
Compare one generated artifact against source data
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow’s profile does not specify residency or retention, while Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs, server filesystem, and provider/tool credentials. If regulated data flows through both, mismatched logging or retention policies can create a compliance gap. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair’s combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF Flowise logging or retention exceeds the policy applied to Airflow artifacts
mitigations: Classify one sample payload before deployment
Disable verbose logging in Flowise
Confirm retention settings for both systems
Avoid sending regulated data through shared flows
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
